newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Sept Fipe inflation at 0.07 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Sept Fipe inflation at 0.07 pct.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) hit a record low in September at 0.07 percent, the lowest rate since December 1958 when the index showed no growth, a Fipe official said.
In August the Fipe inflation index stood at 0.34 percent.
Juarez Rizzieri, president of the Fipe institute, said the inflation rate would rise slightly in October, but by the end of the year should slow to around 0.5 percent.
Rizzieri said the slowing in Fipe inflation resulted from lower clothing and food prices.
He gave the following breakdown of the Fipe weighted index for September.
- Food -0.43 pct fall in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures at weekly intervals.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
